p: South Parade sits right in the middle of Leeds' grand civic quarter. Park Square, just a few steps away, is a lovely Georgian square with a small garden at its centre, perfect for a breather on a sunny lunchtime. Leeds Town Hall, the Victorian landmark with its tall clock tower, is just up the road on the Headrow, and Millennium Square nearby hosts events, outdoor screenings and seasonal markets through the year.

For a group darts night, a couple of tips. Book the right number of players and get there a few minutes early to settle in. If you've got a big group, split into teams across a couple of oches to keep everyone throwing. And decide who's in charge of picking the games, because there are plenty to choose from and indecision eats into your time.

First time at the oche? Stand side-on with your front foot pointing towards the board. Keep your elbow still, lift your forearm and release the dart with a smooth flick. Follow through. Don't try to throw too hard, because accuracy beats power. The scoring tech does the sums, so you just have to aim and enjoy it.

Leeds is famous for its nightlife, and a session here is the perfect start to an evening in town. Afterwards, head to Call Lane or the Calls area for bars and restaurants, or stroll along the river to Granary Wharf. There's never a dull moment in Leeds on a Friday night.
